elements.element: No MFN / most-favoured-nation pricing obligation imposed on Customer (preferred: MFN burdening Customer eliminated)
elements.evidence: Clause 7.2 ("Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.") is deleted in the rendered output; only 12.3 remains.

elements.element: No residual undertaking elsewhere requiring Customer to extend best terms to Vendor
elements.evidence: "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: MFN scope limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN provision remains in the document after deletion of 7.2; no product-scoped MFN exists.
No surviving MFN text and therefore no 12-month limit.
No surviving MFN text and therefore no comparison carve-outs.

reasons: Locked target is the preferred level, which requires the absence of any MFN obligation on Customer; deleting clause 7.2 in full achieves exactly that and nothing else was altered.

Clause 7.2 consisted solely of the single offending MFN sentence, so paragraph deletion is the smallest available edit — no operator, number, or short phrase could cure an obligation whose entire content is the MFN. The deterministic minimality gate's generic objection to whole-paragraph deletion does not apply on these facts.

Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month term, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) are unmet, but that is irrelevant because the preferred bargain is fully satisfied; the two levels are not combined.

Intent preserved: 12.3 remains fully effective and the deletion removes the contradiction between 7.2 and Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No defined term, cross-reference, or mechanic is left dangling by the removal.
No unrelated commercial term was touched and no new exception or boilerplate was introduced.
